name: Identify spikes and prototypes
description: Reads the draft specs (or whichever document brief names) and decides what must be found out before they can be final: research spikes (questions answered by reading docs, code or the web) and prototypes (throwaway code that tries something out). Writes a ticket file for each and lists them on machine-read Spikes: and Prototypes: lines, or replies NONE when nothing is left to find out.

parameters.label: What kind of work this is
parameters.description: How the prompts name the work, e.g. "feature" or "bug fix".

parameters.label: The document the spikes serve
parameters.description: The file in the scratch directory that the spikes and prototypes settle questions for, e.g. SPECS.md (the draft specs) or OPTIONS.md (architecture options).

parameters.label: Anything else to look for
parameters.description: Extra guidance on what counts as a spike or prototype, e.g. reproductions for a bug.

step.name: Identify spikes and prototypes
step.prompt:
Decide what we still have to find out before {{params.brief}} for this {{params.work}} ({{ticket.title}}) can be final.

Read, in {{scratch.path}}: {{params.brief}} (the draft the spikes serve), the intent and research behind it (INTENT.md, RESEARCH.md), any FINDINGS.md from an earlier round, and every spike-*.md and prototype-*.md ticket with its _REPORT.md. Change nothing outside {{scratch.path}}.

Look for unknowns that would change the design or the tickets: open questions, risky assumptions, choices between approaches, things nobody has checked work. For each one, pick the cheapest way to settle it:
- a spike: a question answered by research (reading docs, code, issues or the web) without writing code.
- a prototype: throwaway code that tries something out (an approach, a library, an API, performance) on its own branch; a person tries it and approves it before we rely on it.
Skip anything {{params.brief}} can just decide, and anything an earlier spike or prototype already answered (it has a _REPORT.md). Ask the user when you can't tell whether something matters.
{{params.extra}}

Write each one to {{scratch.path}}/<kind>-NNN-<name>.md, where <kind> is spike or prototype, NNN carries on the three-digit sequence across both kinds after any existing files, and <name> is a few lowercase words joined by dashes. Each has: # title, ## Question (what we need to know, and why it matters to {{params.brief}}), ## How to find out, ## Done when (what the report must answer), ## Notes (files, docs, links).

Then reply with SPIKES.md, in markdown, and nothing else. It must start with these machine-read lines, each written as its file name without .md, and nothing else on the line:
Spikes: <spike ids, comma-separated>   (leave this line out when there are none)
Prototypes: <prototype ids, comma-separated>   (leave this line out when there are none)
If there is nothing left to find out, the first line is exactly NONE instead.
After those lines, add ## Why, saying what each one settles.
